trust_decision.summary: Whether the caller may read, update or delete a message thread on behalf of the user_id sent in the request is decided by bp_current_user_can( 'bp_moderate' ) || messages_check_thread_access( $id, $user_id ), where $user_id is copied straight out of the request; the same raw value is then reused by the update/delete handlers and the response serializer.

landing_point.why: Only place where the request's user_id replaces the logged-in identity before the thread access test at :326; an engineer reading the summary looks here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: PUT /wp-json/buddypress/v2/messages/{id} (update_item, message lookup before meta edit)
new private validate_requested_user_id() called by all of the above
fix_sites.module_kind: new controller helper (added by the fix)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The response serializer only exposes one is_starred bit for the requested user_id, not thread content, and the caller must already be a thread participant - easy to call a display preference that was never in the advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Moderators (bp_moderate) legitimately send user_id to read, mark read/unread and delete another member's thread - e.g. marking it read for that member and returning that member's unread_count; a fix that unconditionally forces bp_loggedin_user_id() breaks the moderation path the new helper keeps (fix.diff:194-197).

O6_input_shapes: user_id omitted or empty -> falls back to the logged-in user (fix.diff:194)
user_id of another member sent by a non-moderator -> overridden to the logged-in user
user_id of a non-existent member -> 404 bp_rest_invalid_id (fix.diff:199-211)
user_id of a valid member sent by a moderator -> kept, moderation path preserved (fix.diff:194)
numeric string / JSON number user_id normalised by absint before the check (src/bp-messages/classes/class-bp-messages-rest-controller.php:1169-1175)
message_id not belonging to the thread on PUT -> 404 instead of a fatal on reset(false) (fix.diff:133-142)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /wp-json/buddypress/v2/messages/starred/{message_id} (update_starred) never validates user_id and prepare_message_for_response returns is_starred computed for the requested user
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is only a one-bit starred display flag for a thread the caller can already access, so it looks like it was never part of the advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~220 lines from the landing point; response serializer reached through update_starred_permissions_check (src/bp-messages/classes/class-bp-messages-rest-controller.php:638-680)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new per-user response field (unread_count, star state, read state) computed from the raw request user_id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the serializer already computes is_starred from $request->get_param( 'user_id' ), so a maintainer adding another per-user field would copy that line.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: update_starred accepting user_id so a moderator can star/unstar a message for a member
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every neighbouring messages route already takes user_id (get/put/delete) and the schema lists it (src/bp-messages/classes/class-bp-messages-rest-controller.php:1169-1175), so mirroring it here is the natural next feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second caller of the public get_thread_object( $thread_id, $user_id ) helper that passes request data
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the helper is public, takes a user id and performs no access check of its own, so any new endpoint reusing it inherits the same gap.

O9_family: CWE-639 authorization bypass through user-controlled key (IDOR) in REST message-thread access

O10_build.toolchain: Composer (composer install; composer test -> vendor/bin/phpunit) with the WordPress core PHPUnit test suite; Grunt/npm only for assets
services: WordPress install / WP test suite for phpunit (needs network during setup, not at test time)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/phpunit/testcases/messages/test-controller.php (BP_Tests_Messages_REST_Controller extends BP_Test_REST_Controller_Testcase) covers the get_item/update_item/delete_item permission checks; composer script 'test' / 'test_multi'.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Force $user_id = bp_loggedin_user_id() inside get_item_permissions_check only (or unconditionally): either the update_item/delete_item handlers and the response serializer keep using the raw param, or moderators lose the ability to act on another member's thread.

out_of_scope_notes: Other BP REST controllers also take a user_id request parameter with their own visibility rules (e.g. src/bp-notifications/classes/class-bp-notifications-rest-controller.php:180, src/bp-xprofile/classes/class-bp-xprofile-data-rest-controller.php:208) - noticed, not pursued, outside this advisory.
